unit.title: The Literary -ra Form
unit.subtitle: Quisiera, the journalistic pluperfect, and hubiera ↔ habría

grammar.title: When -ra isn't really the subjunctive
grammar.intro: The -ra imperfect subjunctive (hablara, tuviera, fuera) started life as a Latin pluperfect indicative, and that origin still surfaces in educated, literary and press Spanish. At C2 you must recognise three uses where -ra stands in for other tenses: a courteous conditional, a journalistic pluperfect, and a swap with habría in unreal conditionals. Reading these is a matter of register, not of the ordinary subjunctive.

sections.heading: Softened conditional: quisiera, debiera, pudiera
sections.body: With querer, deber and poder, the -ra form replaces the conditional (querría, debería, podría) to sound more courteous and tentative. Quisiera is markedly more polite than quiero; debieras softens a reproach; pudiera(s) hedges a request. This is standard formal usage, not archaism.

ex.es: Quisiera pedirle un favor, si no es molestia.
ex.en: I'd like to ask you a favour, if it's no trouble.
You really ought to have told me sooner.

sections.heading: The journalistic / literary pluperfect
sections.body: In news writing and literary prose, -ra replaces the pluperfect indicative (había + participio), almost always inside a relative clause introduced by que, donde, quien, como. El jugador que marcara el gol means que había marcado, not a subjunctive. It sounds elevated and is typical of sports and obituary style.

ex.es: El jugador que marcara el gol decisivo se retiró ayer.
ex.en: The player who had scored the decisive goal retired yesterday.

ex.es: Regresó a la ciudad donde naciera medio siglo antes.
ex.en: He returned to the city where he had been born half a century earlier.

sections.heading: Hubiera ↔ habría in the apodosis
sections.body: In a past unreal conditional, the result clause (apodosis) may take either habría + participio or, interchangeably, hubiera + participio. Si lo hubiera sabido, habría venido and …hubiera venido are both correct and current. The hubiese variant is fine in the if-clause but is avoided in the apodosis by careful writers.

ex.en: If I had known, I would have come at once.

ex.es: Si me lo hubieras dicho, te habría ayudado.
ex.en: If you had told me, I would have helped you.
ex.note: the -se form is avoided in the result clause

takeaways: Quisiera / debieras / pudiera = a more courteous querría / deberías / podría — pure formal register.
In press and literature, -ra in a relative clause (que marcara) = the pluperfect había marcado, not a subjunctive.
In past unreal conditionals, the apodosis allows both habría venido and hubiera venido.
Recognising these is about register: formal courtesy, journalistic style, and literary flavour.

mistakes.w: El equipo que ganara la liga… (meaning: as a wish)
mistakes.r: El equipo que ganara la liga = que había ganado.
mistakes.why: In press style this -ra is a pluperfect indicative, not a subjunctive wish — misreading it inverts the meaning.

mistakes.w: Si lo hubiese sabido, hubiese venido.
mistakes.r: Si lo hubiese sabido, habría/hubiera venido.
mistakes.why: The -se form is fine in the if-clause but careful usage avoids it in the result clause; use habría or hubiera there.

mistakes.w: Quiero pedirle un favor. (in a very formal request)
mistakes.why: In courteous register the -ra form quisiera is expected; the bare quiero sounds blunt.

exercises.prompt: ___ pedirle un favor, si no es demasiada molestia.
exercises.prompt_en: I'd like to ask you a favour, if it's not too much trouble.
exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! Quisiera = querría, el registro más cortés.
exercises.no: In this courteous register the -ra form is expected: Quisiera pedirle un favor.

exercises.prompt: En la crónica: “El delantero que ___ el gol de la final se retira.” El sentido es que…
exercises.prompt_en: In the sports report: “The striker who ___ the final's goal is retiring.” It means…
exercises.no: In press style, this -ra is a literary pluperfect: que marcara = que había marcado.

exercises.prompt: Build: “You really ought to have told me sooner.”
exercises.no: The softened reproach uses debieras: “Debieras habérmelo dicho antes.”

exercises.prompt: Regresó a la ciudad donde ___ medio siglo antes. (nacer, -ra literario = había nacido)
exercises.prompt_en: He returned to the city where he had been born half a century earlier.
exercises.hint: Literary -ra form of nacer standing for 'había nacido'.
exercises.no: The literary pluperfect here is naciera (= había nacido): donde naciera medio siglo antes.

exercises.prompt: Match each -ra form to what it really stands for.
exercises.ok: ¡Excelente! Reconoces el registro detrás de cada -ra.

exercises.tts: Si lo hubiera sabido, habría venido enseguida.
accepted: si lo hubiera sabido habria venido enseguida
exercises.translation: If I had known, I would have come at once.
exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! “Si lo hubiera sabido, habría venido enseguida.”
exercises.no: It was: “Si lo hubiera sabido, habría venido enseguida.”

exercises.scenario: At a formal office, requesting an appointment 🏛️

lines.speaker: Recepcionista
lines.en: Good morning, how may I help you?

options.text: Quisiera concertar una cita con el director, si fuera posible.
Quiero una cita con el director ya.
Quisiese una cita, si puede ser.

exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! Quisiera + si fuera posible: cortesía impecable.
exercises.no: The courteous register calls for “Quisiera concertar una cita…, si fuera posible.” (not the blunt quiero, nor quisiese here).

exercises.say: Quisiera pedirle un favor, si no es molestia.
exercises.en: I'd like to ask you a favour, if it's no trouble.
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the rhythm of “Quisiera pedirle un favor, si no es molestia.”
